prompt:
You are a sceptical financial analyst reviewing a forecast prepared by a colleague.

Given the following forecast for IREDA (base year 2022):
{
  "strategy": "alt_strategy",
  "base_year": 2022,
  "anomaly_detected": true,
  "forecast": [
    {
      "year": 2023,
      "revenue_cr": 3200,
      "net_income_cr": 780,
      "eps": 9.9
    },
    {
      "year": 2024,
      "revenue_cr": 3750,
      "net_income_cr": 950,
      "eps": 12.05
    },
    {
      "year": 2025,
      "revenue_cr": 4350,
      "net_income_cr": 1130,
      "eps": 14.35
    }
  ],
  "top_assumptions": [
    "Loan disbursements will continue to grow at 25-30% CAGR driven by India's renewable energy expansion targets and IREDA's 82% disbursement growth in FY22, translating to sustained interest income growth of ~17-20% per year as the loan book compounds from the \u20b933,256 crore advances base seen at March 2022.",
    "Net Interest Margins and fee income will improve modestly as the loan mix shifts toward short-term loans and new segments (EVs, green hydrogen advisory), while credit costs (impairment charges) normalize from the elevated \u20b9179.90 crore in FY22 as the COVID-restructured book (\u20b92,668.80 lakh) resolves, supporting PAT margins expanding from ~22% in FY22 toward ~26% by FY25."
  ],
  "reasoning": "IREDA is an NBFC; Total Income (Revenue from Operations + Other Income) is used as the top-line revenue: FY22 \u20b92,859.90 + \u20b914.26 = \u20b92,874.16 crore; FY21 \u20b92,654.81 + \u2082.93 = \u20b92,657.74 crore \u2014 a ~8% YoY growth. However, FY22 is anomalous in that sanctions surged 117% and disbursements 82%, which is far above the modest ~7-8% revenue growth seen in FY21-22 (the lag between disbursements hitting the loan book and interest income recognition means FY23-25 revenues will see accelerated catch-up). Additionally, a \u20b91,500 crore equity infusion in FY22 materially expanded the balance sheet, supporting much higher lending capacity. Given the disbursement surge represents leading indicators for interest income (typical 6-12 month lag), the 3-year CAGR of ~8% is not the right basis; instead a mean-reversion recovery toward 17-20% revenue growth is used for FY23, stepping up as the enlarged loan book seasons. PAT growth is projected to outpace revenue growth as impairment charges normalise and operating leverage improves; EPS is computed on approximately 787 crore shares (post the \u20b91,500 crore equity contribution at face value of \u20b910 implying ~150 crore new shares added to an estimated prior base of ~637 crore shares, giving ~787 crore total shares)."
}

Step 1: Identify the 3 most critical assumptions embedded in this forecast.
Step 2: For each assumption, describe one plausible scenario where it fails.
Step 3: Rate each assumption failure as Low / Medium / High risk to the forecast accuracy.
Step 4: Assign an overall confidence score from 0-100 (100 = completely certain).

RESPONSE FORMAT: Begin your response DIRECTLY with the opening brace { — no reasoning or text before the JSON.

Return ONLY valid JSON:
{
  "company": "<COMPANY>",
  "base_year": <YYYY>,
  "strategy": "<baseline|alt_strategy>",
  "assumptions": [
    {"assumption": "<text>", "failure_scenario": "<text>", "risk": "<Low|Medium|High>"}
  ],
  "confidence_score": <0-100>,
  "overall_critique": "<2 sentences>"
}
